page.title: Kestrel Porch Cam — overnight on battery

blocks.heading: Kestrel Porch Cam: one night on battery, and a late package push when Wi-Fi is down
text: Source: *HLD: Kestrel Porch Cam — overnight on battery* (reviewed design, Kestrel Home platform team; local file, unversioned), the approved Backstage catalog snapshot and the approved reviewed code locations, plus the operator's answers. Engineering level: every service hop, catalog API operation and code reference.

Illustrative: minutes not given by the operator (bedtime heartbeat 10:30 PM, the 7:00 AM charging heartbeat, 8:07 AM clip opened, Wi-Fi retry at 8:09 AM, reconnect at 8:15 AM), the values of scheduled heartbeats between lit steps, and the solar charge rate of 3.5 %/h (midpoint of the HLD's 3–4 %/h). Idle drain 1 %/h and about 1 % per clip are from the HLD.

Tension: at the HLD's ~1 %/h idle drain, 25 % at 10:30 PM minus one clip reaches 20 % near 2:30 AM, not at the operator's 4:00 AM low-battery heartbeat. Both anchors are kept: the camera battery is held at 24 % after the 1:10 AM clip and set to the reported 20 % at 4:00 AM; the stated rate applies again from 4:00 AM.

sources.label: device-shadow
sources.detail: Last heartbeat: battery %, charging, online. The HLD does not say when the app fetches it.

steps.text: 10:30 PM Thu. The resident goes to bed. Scheduled 30-minute heartbeat: the Porch Cam sends battery **25%**, charging **no** over Wi-Fi to `event-ingest` (`POST /heartbeats`), which writes it to `device-shadow`. Camera online, Wi-Fi good, no notifications on the phone.

codeRefs.label: heartbeat route
codeRefs.purpose: Accepts a heartbeat and writes battery/charging to device-shadow

steps.text: 1:10 AM Fri. A raccoon crosses the porch. PIR wakes the camera; it records a ~20 s clip (about 1% battery) and uploads it: `POST /events` to `event-ingest`, the clip to `clip-store` (`PUT /clips/{clipId}`). `event-ingest` asks `motion-classifier` for a label: **animal**. Animal events are saved to the timeline with **no push** (default user setting), so nothing goes to `notify-service`. The app's last heartbeat is the scheduled 1:00 AM one (illustrative).

batt.note: held at 25% until the clip (see tension note)

steps.text: 4:00 AM. The 4:00 AM heartbeat reports battery **20%**. `device-shadow` marks the camera `low_battery` (at or below 20%) and triggers one push: `notify-service` sends **Porch Cam battery low** through APNs/FCM. It will not send it again until the battery goes above 30%.

steps.text: 6:50 AM. Sunrise: the solar panel starts producing power and the camera begins charging. Nothing is reported yet: `device-shadow` and the app still hold the scheduled 6:30 AM heartbeat (about 18%, not charging; illustrative). The app lags the device.

7:00 AM. The next heartbeat reports charging **yes** (battery about 18%). `event-ingest` writes it to `device-shadow`; the app's device page now shows the solar charging icon. Still at or below 30%, so `low_battery` stays set and no second low-battery push is sent.

codeRefs.label: heartbeat route
codeRefs.purpose: Accepts a heartbeat and writes battery/charging to device-shadow

steps.text: 8:05 AM. A courier drops a package. The camera records a clip (about 1%) and uploads it: `POST /events`, clip to `clip-store`. `motion-classifier` labels it **package**; `event-ingest` forwards it to `notify-service`, which pushes **Package delivered at front door** through APNs/FCM. The app's last heartbeat is the scheduled 8:00 AM one (about 21%, charging; illustrative).

steps.text: 8:07 AM. The resident opens the clip in the Kestrel app. The device page shows the 8:00 AM heartbeat: 21%, solar charging, online. The HLD does not describe how the app fetches the clip or the device state, so no read is drawn.

codeRefs.label: DevicePage
codeRefs.purpose: Device page: battery %, charging icon, 'updated <time>', online/offline

steps.text: 8:05 AM. Home Wi-Fi is down when the courier drops the package. The camera records the clip (about 1%) but cannot reach the router, so it keeps the clip on its **SD card** and retries every 2 minutes. No event reaches `event-ingest`: no label, no push. `device-shadow` still holds the 8:00 AM heartbeat (illustrative: Wi-Fi dropped after it).

8:09 AM. The 2-minute retries (8:07, 8:09) still fail; the clip stays queued on the SD card. The app still shows the last state with an older "updated" time. `device-shadow` does **not** mark the camera offline: that needs two missed heartbeats (60 minutes).

8:15 AM. Wi-Fi returns about 10 minutes later. The camera uploads the queued clip (`POST /events`, clip to `clip-store` as a late upload) and sends a heartbeat (about 21%, charging). `motion-classifier` labels the clip **package**.
